title: Manufacture and Drug Delivery Applications of Silk Nanoparticles
protocol: Cut 5 g of dried cocoons into 5 mm x 5 mm pieces.
Remove soiled layers from the cut cocoon pieces.
Weigh out 4.24 g of sodium carbonate.
Add sodium carbonate carefully to 2 L of boiling distilled water.
Boil cut cocoon pieces in the sodium carbonate solution for 60 min.
Stir silk occasionally during boiling to ensure homogenous sample processing.
Remove degummed silk from the solution and wash with 1 L of distilled water for 20 min.
Repeat washing step at least three times.
Squeeze washed silk well to remove excess liquid.
Untie or pull silk by hand after washing.
Place untied silk in a fume hood to air dry overnight.
Weigh out 5 g of air-dried degummed silk fibers the next day.
Pack silk tightly into the bottom of a 50 ml beaker.
Prepare a fresh 9.3 M LiBr solution.
Dissolve silk fibers in LiBr using a 1 g silk to 4 ml LiBr ratio.
Cover the silk LiBr sample with aluminum foil to prevent evaporation.
Allow silk to dissolve completely at 60 °C, occasionally stirring.
This dissolution step takes up to 4 hr.
Wet a dialysis cassette in water for 5 min.
Inject 15 ml of silk LiBr solution into the dialysis cassette and remove air bubbles using a needle and syringe.
Dialyze against 1 L of distilled water, changing the water at 1, 3, and 6 hours on the first day, twice on the second day, and once on the third day.
Collect the silk solution from the dialysis cassette and centrifuge for 20 min at 5 °C at 9,500 x g.
Recover the supernatant and repeat the centrifugation process twice more.
Determine the weight of an empty weighing boat (W1).
Add 1 ml of the silk solution to the weighing boat and record the new weight (W2).
Dry the sample by leaving the weighing boat at 60 °C overnight.
Determine the total dry weight (W3) after drying.
Calculate the concentration of the silk solution using the formula: % = ((W3-W1)/(W2-W1)) x 100.
Add a 5% (w/v) silk solution dropwise to acetone while maintaining a >75% (v/v) acetone solution.
For example, add 9 ml of a 5% (w/v) silk solution at a rate of 50 drops/min (10 µl/drop).
Centrifuge the precipitate at 48,000 x g for 2 hours at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in distilled water using a spatula.
Remove the pellet from the spatula with pipet tips.
Vortex for 20 seconds.
Sonicate at 30% amplitude for 30 seconds, repeating twice.
Top up the centrifuge tube to capacity with distilled water.
Repeat the centrifugation and resuspension steps at least twice.
Resuspend the final pellet in 6 ml of distilled water.
Store the suspension at 4 °C until use.
Centrifuge silk nanoparticles at 48,000 x g for 2 hours at 4 °C.
Collect all nanoparticles in 3 ml of distilled water.
Sonicate at 30% amplitude for 30 seconds, repeating twice.
Divide the 3 ml stock into 2 ml and 1 ml lots.
Transfer the 2 ml sample into a pre-weighed tube.
Record the total weight of the 2 ml sample.
Store the 1 ml lot at 4 °C until use.
Snap freeze and then lyophilize the 2 ml silk nanoparticle lot overnight in a freeze dryer.
Reweigh the 2 ml tube after freeze-drying.
Calculate the amount of silk nanoparticles (mg) originally present in the 2 ml sample.
Dilute the 1 ml silk nanoparticle stock with distilled water to generate a calibration curve (0.04-7 mg/ml).
Ensure that samples do not exceed the absorbance maximum.
Measure the absorbance of each standard dilution at 600 nm using a 96-well plate setup.
Plot absorbance versus concentration (mg/ml) for the standard curve.
Use this standard curve routinely to determine the concentration of silk nanoparticles in suspensions.
Dissolve 1.2 mg of doxorubicin HCl in 8 ml distilled water.
Make up to 10 ml with distilled water to yield a working stock of 116 µg/ml (0.2 µmol/ml).
Mix 2 ml of 0.2 µmol/ml doxorubicin solution with 200 µl of 10, 30 or 50 mg/ml of silk nanoparticles in a 2 ml tube.
Incubate the silk-doxorubicin suspension at room temperature (25 °C) overnight on a rotating mixer.
Centrifuge the silk-doxorubicin suspension at 194,000 x g for 30 min.
Wash the doxorubicin-loaded silk nanoparticles with distilled water and repeat this procedure twice more.
Pool the supernatant and note the total volume.
Resuspend the doxorubicin-loaded silk nanoparticles in distilled water, protect from light and store at 4 ºC until use.
Pipette 200 µl of supernatant into a black microtiter plate.
Measure doxorubicin-associated fluorescence using a fluorescence microplate reader at an excitation wavelength of 485 nm and emission wavelength of 590 nm.
Generate a calibration curve for doxorubicin based on the measured fluorescence values.
Calculate the concentration of doxorubicin in the supernatant using the calibration curve.
Repeat measurements three independent times.
Determine encapsulation efficiency using equation (1).
Store silk nanoparticles in distilled water at 4 °C and 25 °C.
Measure size and zeta potential of silk nanoparticles on days 0, 14, and 28 using dynamic light scattering (DLS).
Set refractive indices to 1.33 for distilled water and 1.60 for protein.
Calculate particle sizes with the user interface software.
Conduct morphological assessment of silk nanoparticles by scanning electron microscopy (SEM).
Place a carbon adhesive disc onto an SEM stub.
Attach a silicon wafer to the SEM stub.
Dilute silk nanoparticles to a concentration of 1 mg/ml.
Pipette 10 μl of the diluted sample onto a silicon wafer.
Freeze the sample at -80 °C.
Lyophilize the frozen sample overnight using a freeze drying system.
Coat the lyophilized sample with a gold layer up to 20 nm thick.
Image samples with a scanning electron microscope at 5 kV and a 40,000-fold magnification.
Culture MDA-MB-231 cells in RPMI 1640 containing 10% v/v FBS.
Plate MDA-MB-231 cells on tissue culture treated polystyrene.
Incubate the plates in a humidified 5% CO2 atmosphere at 37 °C.
Subculture cells routinely when they reach 80% confluence every 2−3 days.
Plate MDA-MB-231 cells at a density of 2 x 10^4 cells/cm^2 in 96-well plates.
Allow the cells to recover overnight.
Add 0.001-1 µg freely diffusible doxorubicin into 96-well plates (final volume 100 μl per well).
Add 0.001-0.5 mg silk nanoparticles into 96-well plates (final volume 100 μl per well).
Add 0.1 mg silk nanoparticles loaded with 0.001-1 µg doxorubicin into 96-well plates (final volume 100 μl per well).
Determine cell viability and IC50 by adding MTT at a concentration of 5 mg/ml in PBS at 72 hours.
Incubate for 5 hours.
Drain the wells carefully with a pipette.
Dissolve the formazan crystals with 100 μl of dimethyl sulfoxide.
Measure the absorbance at 560 nm.
Repeat the measurement in three independent experiments.
Seed MDA-MB-231 cells on sterile glass coverslips at a density of 2 x 10^4 cells/cm².
Allow the cells to recover overnight.
Expose the cells to the desired treatment conditions for 72 hours.
Fix the cells with 2% v/v glutaraldehyde in PBS for 30 minutes.
Wash the samples twice with distilled water.
Dehydrate the samples using an ethanol series.
Critical point dry the samples as detailed elsewhere.
Sputter coat the samples with a gold layer up to 20 nm thick using a low vacuum sputter coater.
Image the samples by SEM using an electron acceleration of 5 kV and 700-fold magnification.
